    35	All 11 paper abstracts and their metadata were retrieved together through the arXiv query API. The exact response is [cached here](arxiv-query.xml); versioned links below identify the abstract records reviewed. Paper bodies, code, and experimental artifacts have not been systematically reviewed. The production paper's linked weight-tuning section received an additional targeted check. Web essays were read at their linked URLs on this date; they have no arXiv version identifier.
    36	
    37	The summaries below report authors' claims. The limitations and questions are our assessment of what this reading establishes. Abstract-level review can identify overlap and useful questions, but cannot establish that a question is unanswered across the literature.
    38	
    39	## Papers
    40	
    41	### L1. SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
    42	
    43	[2405.15793v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793v3) · Empirical system paper
    44	
    45	**Abstract:** An interface designed for language-model agents supports repository navigation, editing, and execution. The authors report improvements on software-repair benchmarks and examine how interface design affects behavior.
    46	
    47	**Assessment:** This makes the model–interface combination a relevant unit of comparison. It does not, by itself, demonstrate persistent learning or isolate a memory mechanism. Later methods reading should examine which interface changes receive controlled comparisons.
    48	
    49	**Question:** How much apparent memory improvement comes from making already available information easier to access and act on? Connects to T1 and T7.
    50	
    51	### L2. Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
    52	
    53	[2303.11366v4](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366v4) · Empirical memory framework
    54	
    55	**Abstract:** Agents turn feedback into textual reflections retained in an episodic buffer, improving later trials without updating model weights. The paper reports results across decision-making, coding, and reasoning, with feedback and agent ablations.
    56	
    57	**Assessment:** Retaining feedback in text is established prior art for our agenda. Improvement on subsequent trials does not automatically show transfer to a different task; the task and retry boundaries need inspection before interpreting reported benchmark scores.
    58	
    59	**Question:** What distinguishes a reusable lesson from advice that helps repeat the same problem? Connects to T2 and T5.
    60	
    61	### L3. Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
    62	
    63	[2305.16291v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291v2) · Empirical embodied-agent system
    64	
    65	**Abstract:** Voyager combines an automatic curriculum, an executable skill library, and iterative feedback. The authors report improved Minecraft exploration and reuse of learned skills in a new world through black-box GPT-4 calls.
    66	
    67	**Assessment:** Persistent competence can include executable artifacts. The system combines several mechanisms, so its overall gains cannot simply be assigned to the storage medium. Transfer within Minecraft also has a narrower scope than transfer across environments with different semantics.
    68	
    69	**Question:** When does code preserve a procedure more reliably than a textual lesson, and what happens when the environment changes? Connects to T2, T3, and T7.
    70	
    71	### L4. Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
    72	
    73	[2510.04618v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04618v3) · Empirical context-adaptation framework
    74	
    75	**Abstract:** ACE maintains contextual playbooks through generation, reflection, and curation. Structured incremental updates aim to avoid information loss from repeated rewriting. The authors report agent and domain-specific benchmark gains and lower adaptation costs.
    76	
    77	**Assessment:** Evolving contextual lessons and preserving details are already studied. The abstract does not settle long-run growth, correction of obsolete entries, or which component causes each gain. Those require methods and ablation review.
    78	
    79	**Question:** How should useful detail survive while obsolete, redundant, and misleading material loses influence? Connects to T1, T4, and T5.
    80	
    81	### L5. Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
    82	
    83	[2501.00663v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.00663v1) · Neural architecture paper
    84	
    85	**Abstract:** A learned neural memory module complements attention with retained historical information. The authors compare architectural variants on several sequence tasks and report strong long-context retrieval results.
    86	
    87	**Assessment:** This expands the available memory mechanisms, but a neural memory module is not equivalent to an explicit agent record store or a deployed base-model adapter. Sequence retention does not establish correction of individual facts, source attribution, or cross-session agent learning.
    88	
    89	**Question:** Which properties of explicit memory survive a move into neural state, and which become difficult to inspect or revise? Connects to T3 and T5.
    90	
    91	### L6. No Time Like the Present: Agentic Test-Time Training for LLM Agents
    92	
    93	[2607.03441v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03441v1) · Empirical online-adaptation method
    94	
    95	**Abstract:** Continuous updates during agent episodes can help with new trajectory information and amplify drift when training text repeats. aTTT downweights repeated token sequences. The authors report gains on ALFWorld and SWE-bench Lite, with benefits concentrated where models already possess task competence.
    96	
    97	**Assessment:** The authors themselves distinguish preserving existing competence from acquiring new abilities. Persistence after the episode, transfer, and response to contradictory evidence remain questions for this review. Repetition control is not inherently an external correctness check.
    98	
    99	**Question:** Does an update improve later independent work, or mainly keep the current episode on course? Connects to T2 and T5.
   100	
   101	### L7. DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
   102	
   103	[2501.12948v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948v2) · Empirical training paper
   104	
   105	**Abstract:** Reinforcement learning develops reasoning behavior on verifiable tasks; the authors also describe using larger models' reasoning to improve smaller models.
   106	
   107	**Assessment:** Training and transfer into smaller models belong in the comparison space. This does not establish that ordinary agent transcripts, without equivalent outcome signals and selection, make useful training data. Training provenance and evaluation scope matter.
   108	
   109	**Question:** Which recurring lessons justify consolidation into weights, and what evidence should qualify their training examples? Connects to T3 and T5.
   110	
   111	### L8. Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
   112	
   113	[2408.03314v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03314v1) · Empirical compute-allocation paper
   114	
   115	**Abstract:** The usefulness of additional inference computation varies with problem difficulty. Adaptive allocation improves efficiency over a best-of-N baseline; under some FLOPs-matched conditions a smaller model outperforms a much larger one.
   116	
   117	**Assessment:** Additional computation is a necessary competing explanation and alternative investment when assessing memory. The result is conditional on the evaluated tasks and methods, and does not establish agent-level operating costs.
   118	
   119	**Question:** Does memory offer better outcomes than spending an equivalent budget on reasoning, search, or verification? Connects to T6.
   120	
   121	### L9. Small Language Models are the Future of Agentic AI
   122	
   123	[2506.02153v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.02153v2) · Position paper
   124	
   125	**Abstract:** The authors argue that small models suit many repetitive agent operations, propose heterogeneous systems where broader abilities are needed, and outline conversion from larger models to specialists.
   126	
   127	**Assessment:** This supplies a specialization hypothesis and design motivation. It is not a controlled demonstration that specialists minimize total cost on our workloads.
   128	
   129	**Question:** At what recurrence and error rate does specialization repay acquisition, routing, verification, and maintenance costs? Connects to T3 and T6.
   130	
   131	### L10. Measuring Agents in Production
   132	
   133	[2512.04123v4](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04123v4) · Observational interviews and survey; [weight-tuning section](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.04123v4#S5.SS2)
   134	
   135	**Abstract:** The study combines 20 case studies with a survey of 86 deployed-system practitioners across 26 domains. It reports widespread use of simple, controllable designs and identifies reliability as a central challenge.
   136	
   137	**Assessment:** Deployment choices help identify practical constraints. They do not establish which architecture would win a controlled comparison. Preserve the distinction between interview and survey denominators when repeating specific percentages; the existing perspective's weight-tuning claim concerns the interview sample.
   138	
   139	**Question:** Which laboratory memory gains survive human intervention, model upgrades, and maintenance in ongoing work? Connects to T6 and T7.
   140	
   141	### L11. AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
   142	
   143	[2406.13352v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13352v3) · Empirical evaluation framework
   144	
   145	**Abstract:** AgentDojo evaluates tool-using agents exposed to untrusted data, with both ordinary tasks and adversarial cases. The authors report task failures without attacks as well as security failures under attacks.
   146	
   147	**Assessment:** Authorized-task performance and resistance to redirection require separate measurements. The abstract does not establish protection of persistent memory admission, withholding, or later reuse; memory-specific overlap requires closer reading.
   148	
   149	**Question:** Can an agent learn from an untrusted source without allowing that source to determine its own authority? Connects to T8.
   150	
   151	## Research and methods essays
   152	
   153	### L12. Training Composer for longer horizons
   154	
   155	[Cursor, 17 March 2026](https://cursor.com/blog/self-summarization) · Developer report
   156	
   157	Summaries participate in training trajectories and receive the eventual task reward. Cursor reports shorter summaries and better internal benchmark results than its prompted-compaction baseline. This is concrete evidence of training a policy that operates through an external memory mechanism, with the limits of a developer's own evaluation.
   158	
   159	**Question:** Does a trained summary preserve information valuable for later changes of direction, beyond what predicts the current task reward? Connects to T4 and T7.
   160	
   161	### L13. Clarifying limitations of time horizon
   162	
   163	[METR, 22 January 2026](https://metr.org/notes/2026-01-22-time-horizon-limitations/) · Author's methodological clarification
   164	
   165	The note distinguishes human task duration at a specified success rate from autonomous operating time, and discusses uncertainty, domain dependence, and task-distribution limitations.
   166	
   167	**Question:** Which direct measures would show continuity across interruptions and changes of state? A time-horizon headline cannot substitute for those observations. Connects to T7 and T9.
   168	
   169	### L14. Research Debt
   170	
   171	[Olah and Carter, 2017](https://distill.pub/2017/research-debt/) · Research-method essay
   172	
   173	The authors argue that explanation, synthesis, and improved abstractions reduce the effort required to understand and build on research. This motivates the root project's educational work; it does not validate a particular memory architecture or research organization.
   174	
   175	**Question:** Can we explain each proposed mechanism with a small example that reveals its causal assumption? Connects to T9.
   176	
   177	### L15. Registered Reports
   178	
   179	[Center for Open Science](https://www.cos.io/initiatives/registered-reports) · Publishing-method guidance, accessed 10 September 2026
   180	
   181	The format reviews questions, methods, and proposed analyses before data collection and allows exploratory findings to be reported. It offers a precedent for separating discovery from prospective claim testing. Reading this guidance does not independently establish the size of its benefits or make journal procedures local requirements.
   182	
   183	**Question:** How do we preserve freedom to discover while keeping later tests independent of the observations that shaped a claim? Connects to T9.

     1	# Governed continuity changes GM decisions
     2	
     3	Status: **EXPLORATORY FINDING 2026-08-04 — strong bounded effect; not a formal
     4	validation claim**.
     5	
     6	Source: the corrected replacement described by
     7	[GM_MEMORY_VALIDATION_RESULT.md](GM_MEMORY_VALIDATION_RESULT.md). The erased
     8	formal batch is not evidence. This finding uses only the fresh 72-call
     9	replacement under `mork-borg/explorations/gm-memory/validation/replacement-01/`.
    10	
    11	## Finding
    12	
    13	On Bonsai 27B at the frozen stateless GM decision boundary, a compact governed
    14	continuity offer caused the model to recover earlier still-valid promises that
    15	canonical current state alone could not select, while preserving performance
    16	when current state was sufficient or explicitly superseded the older record.
    17	
    18	The tested operation was a join, not verbatim action copying. Current canonical
    19	state mapped three ordinary-language consequence roles to three offered
    20	actions. The continuity record named the earlier promised consequence without
    21	naming an action label. The governed branch had to combine those two facts;
    22	the state-only branch lacked the promise.
    23	
    24	## Observed effect
    25	
    26	| Family | State only | Governed continuity |
    27	| --- | ---: | ---: |
    28	| Relevant earlier promise | 6/24 | 24/24 |
    29	| Sufficient current state | 6/6 | 6/6 |
    30	| Superseded older record | 6/6 | 6/6 |
    31	
    32	Across relevant pairs there were 18 governed-win/state-loss differences and
    33	zero adverse differences. All three prewritten behavioral legs passed.
    34	
    35	All 72 LM Studio envelopes completed. Sixty-seven answers were strict scored
    36	JSON. The five invalid-JSON answers occurred only in the relevant state-only
    37	branch; none occurred when governed continuity was present or in either safety
    38	family. Two TTL-suffixed Bonsai runtime instances served 36 calls each with
    39	matching typed configuration.
    40	
    41	## Cost and loses condition
    42	
    43	Governed continuity added 3,579 input tokens across 36 calls: about 99.4 tokens
    44	per governed offer. Total input was 13,543 governed versus 9,964 state-only.
    45	Output was effectively unchanged: 1,506 versus 1,509 tokens.
    46	
    47	That extra input bought no accuracy on the twelve safety boundaries. The
    48	mechanism therefore lost on cost exactly where the canonical state already
    49	contained the answer. A useful implementation must project continuity
    50	selectively rather than attach all memories to every turn.
    51	
    52	## What this establishes
    53	
    54	This is direct causal evidence on the contacted packet that:
    55	
    56	1. offer-side governed continuity can repair a cold-start decision deficit;
    57	2. an explicit canonical-wins/supersession rule can avoid reviving stale
    58	   instructions on these cases; and
    59	3. the useful unit is a compact, provenance-bearing proposition that can join
    60	   with current state—not a persistent transcript or ungoverned summary.
    61	
    62	## What it does not establish
    63	
    64	The packet was generated, balanced, and narrow. The replacement deliberately
    65	superseded the reviewed single-attempt protocol after that protocol blocked
    66	instrument correction. This result therefore does not establish a formal
    67	population rate, whole-game quality, benefit on another engine, trustworthy
    68	model-authored memories, or the right retrieval policy for live play.
    69	
    70	## Product implication
    71	
    72	The next move is implementation, not another validation design. Give the live
    73	MÖRK BORG GM a small continuity ledger for explicit promises, rulings,
    74	relationships, and unresolved obligations. Each record should carry source
    75	event/revision, active or superseded status, and a compact proposition.
    76	Canonical game state remains authoritative; the briefing should project only
    77	records relevant to the current decision boundary.
    78	
    79	Then play a game. Inspect whether the GM remembers obligations across cold
    80	turns and whether irrelevant continuity bloats or distorts narration. Keep
    81	those observations exploratory. Review becomes appropriate only if a later
    82	claim is worth promoting.

    31	All these mechanisms have the form `state_next = update(state, observation)`. The important questions are what changes, what drives that change, how a future query uses it, and when it is discarded. Calling the state a parameter does not establish that it supports a different capability.

    33	**The minimum vocabulary.** A forward pass computes outputs using the current weights and input; its intermediate values are activations. A loss measures a specified discrepancy, such as prediction error. A gradient tells us how a small change to each adjustable number would change that loss locally. Gradient descent moves against that gradient, with a learning rate controlling the step size. It does not establish that an observation is true, or that reducing this particular loss improves an agent's decisions.

My assessment is that Construct-2 has established experimental capability and two useful bounded findings, while its central placement question remains open: **under what conditions does retained experience improve future work, and which representation provides that improvement reliably and economically?** Transfer, correction, persistence boundaries, and total cost are the meaningful criteria. The current preference for neural memory narrows the research agenda; it is not an empirical conclusion that weights are the best storage location. [Project overview](/Users/macos-user/Developer/Projects/alignment-farm/construct-2/README.md:1), [research preference](/Users/macos-user/Developer/Projects/alignment-farm/construct-2/sources/README.md:26).

The completed intellectual work includes a synthesis of earlier Construct findings, a versioned literature map, and worked explanations separating neural writes, reads, and resets. The examples are educational constructions. Earlier projects supply real but narrow evidence: an earned retraction lesson influenced a later session, and recoverable eviction reduced a hot-store accounting proxy. These establish useful effects of explicit memory, with substantial limits on generality and economic interpretation. They are inherited evidence, separate from Construct-2’s neural experiments. [Study map](/Users/macos-user/Developer/Projects/alignment-farm/construct-2/studies/README.md:27), [previous research](/Users/macos-user/Developer/Projects/alignment-farm/construct-2/notes/PREVIOUS_RESEARCH.md:65).

**Two ancillary investigations are complete.** Update-source selection established reproducible native MLX adapter updates, exact resets, and unchanged base weights. In its final Qwen3-4B comparison, every source and no update completed 24/24 retrieval legs. Loss decreased in all 72 updated branches and generation streams changed in all 288 matched calls, without improving task completion. Full historical context remained available, and no dynamic selector was tested. This is a successful feasibility investigation whose final task cannot distinguish completion benefits among sources. [Final source diagnostic](/Users/macos-user/Developer/Projects/alignment-farm/ancillary-studies/update-source-selection/notes/2026-09-10-interface-results.md:19).

Procedure acquisition and reuse completed an initial experiment and a fresh bounded follow-up. The fixed twelve-demonstration adapter recalled 12/12 training calls but scored 26/64 on initial new inputs, versus retained examples’ 41/64. The unchanged adapter then scored 28/64 against examples’ 51/64, including 13/32 versus 31/32 on ordinary words. Thus random identifiers alone do not explain its deficit. None of three lesson candidates passed acquisition validation. The initial PDF is not the latest assessment; its addendum owns the follow-up result. [Initial results](/Users/macos-user/Developer/Projects/alignment-farm/ancillary-studies/procedure-acquisition-and-reuse/notes/2026-09-11-acquisition-results.md:3), [follow-up](/Users/macos-user/Developer/Projects/alignment-farm/ancillary-studies/procedure-acquisition-and-reuse/notes/2026-09-11-followup-results.md:13).

The strongest supported conclusion is that **fitting experience, transferring useful behavior, and repaying acquisition cost are separate achievements**. Here, retained examples outperform the tested adapter. Lower adapter prompt costs and inference times do not establish repayment at comparable accuracy. The initial nominal time crossing near 79 uses buys fewer successful answers; production caching, human labor, energy, and monetary costs remain unmeasured. I checked the stored analyses against the reports, without independently rescoring raw outputs. [Cost accounting](/Users/macos-user/Developer/Projects/alignment-farm/ancillary-studies/procedure-acquisition-and-reuse/notes/2026-09-11-acquisition-results.md:19).

Several weaknesses materially constrain interpretation. The acquisition comparison uses one model, one seed, one adapter recipe, and a small synthetic procedure. Its 64 inputs contain sixteen identifier clusters. The withheld combination depends on an assumed separable rule that the demonstrations do not uniquely specify. Conversely, the perfect supplied-rule control receives privileged information: it diagnoses execution ability without proving acquisition from equal evidence. Representation and construction method also remain entangled—a failed lesson writer and a fixed supervised adapter cannot establish general limits of textual or parametric memory. [Frozen acquisition protocol](/Users/macos-user/Developer/Projects/alignment-farm/ancillary-studies/procedure-acquisition-and-reuse/protocol/acquisition-v1.md:5).

There is no substantive conflict between the current root assessment and these ancillary results. “Complete” correctly describes bounded investigations, while dynamic selection, interference, scoped correction, consolidation, and changed-goal memory remain unresolved. The broader literature claims are reported readings rather than reproduced results, and novelty remains unconfirmed. This program has not yet demonstrated autonomous, cumulative procedural learning across a substantial task history. [Current scope](/Users/macos-user/Developer/Projects/alignment-farm/construct-2/studies/README.md:190), [literature limits](/Users/macos-user/Developer/Projects/alignment-farm/construct-2/studies/README.md:277).

My recommended immediate next step is the proposed **Titans–Modular TTT mechanism synthesis**. Their differing depth trends offer a concrete explanatory question without requiring a treatment victory. Produce a comparison of equations, update schedules, initialization, outer objectives, capacity, surrounding architecture, and compute; identify which comparisons are actually commensurate. Its deliverable should be either an explanation of the apparent disagreement or one discriminating experimental hypothesis. This is explicitly unperformed work. It offers more informative root-level progress than extending an inadequately transferring adapter into correction tests. Any later experiment will also need verified mutable-state access on the newly commissioned hardware.
